senses.def: A common offensive formation, beginning with the usual five offensive linemen (two offensive tackles, two guards, and a center), the quarterback under center, and two backs in-line behind the quarterback. The base variant adds a tight end to one side of the line and two wide receivers, one at each end of the line.
A formation in doubles where the server's partner starts crouched down close to the center of the net
Implementation Force (IFOR), a NATO-led multinational peacekeeping force in Bosnia and Herzegovina in the mid-1990s
A settlement in Plaistow parish, Chichester district, West Sussex, England (OS grid ref TQ0231).

senses.def: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see if, only.
ex: It made me feel better, if only for a moment.
It won't be much fun if only guys turn up to the party.

senses.def: I wish that; would (that) (archaic). Signifies a wish or desire for the present or the future.
ex: If only I could win the lottery.
My gambling ex could come to his senses, if only.

senses.def: I wish that; would (that) (archaic). Signifies a regret about an action in the past.
ex: If only I had listened to my parents.
We didn't have that luxury. If only!

senses.def: Even if for no other reason than; only just.
ex: I was pretty sure what I wanted, but I still tried on another if only to make sure.

senses.def: Signifies a hypothetical or wishful precondition, or one which would be simple but is nonetheless unlikely, for a hypothetical, counterfactual, or future outcome.
ex: He could be a great student if only he got [or: if he only got] a little non-judgmental encouragement.
If you'd only quit interrupting me, I'll tell you!

senses.def: If only somebody at the top of an abusive hierarchy were aware of the abuses, they would take action to stop them.
A particular drug used in chemotherapy.
